{{nihongo|'''Atago Shrine'''|愛宕神社|Atago-jinja|qq=}} is a [[Shinto]] {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} on {{ill|Mount Atago|en|Mount Atago|qid=Q2975204|lt=Mount Atago|1=Mount Atago}}, the northwest of {{ill|Kyoto|en|Kyoto|qid=Q34600|lt=Kyoto|1=Kyoto}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}. Enshrined is [[Atago Gongen]] who protects Kyoto from fire.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.city.kyoto.jp/koho/eng/preview/20.html |title=Atago Stone Lanterns |publisher={{ill|Kyoto|en|Kyoto|qid=Q34600|lt=Kyoto City|1=Kyoto}} |accessdate=7 April 2011|qq=}}</ref> [[Shugendō]] practices and a place for worship are known from the eighth century.<ref name="Jinja">{{cite web|url=http://atagojinjya.jp/goyuisyo.htm |title=Atago Jinja - history |publisher=Atago Jinja |accessdate=7 April 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm |archivedate=17 May 2011 |qq=}}</ref> The late-{{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|qid=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period|1=Kamakura period}} [[Honden]] has been designated an {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/1985 |title=Database of Registered National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=7 April 2011|qq=}}</ref> (Actually, the late-Kamakura period Honden is located at another Atago-jinja in [[:en:Kameoka|Kameoka]], to the northwest of Kyoto : {{Coord|35|2|28|N|135|35|13|E||qq=}}[http://wikimapia.org/#lat=35.0408446&lon=135.5869369&z=17&l=0&m=b&v=8&show=/26233643/Atago-jinja-Shrine]) Atago Jinja is the head of nine hundred Atago shrines throughout Japan.<ref name="Jinja"/>
